# 11. Configuration artefacts

## 11.1 nftables (generated by the agent, illustrative)

```
table inet useg {
    set lan4     { type ipv4_addr; flags interval; elements = { 192.168.100.0/24 } }
    set router4  { type ipv4_addr; elements = { 192.168.100.1 } }
    set blocked4 { type ipv4_addr; flags interval; }
    set devbytes { type ipv4_addr; counter; }   # per-device raw bytes, drift report only

    chain prerouting {
        type filter hook prerouting priority mangle; policy accept;

        # the box itself is always reachable (DNS, portal, subscription, VLESS)
        ip daddr 192.168.100.2 accept

        # local-only destinations are never proxied or metered
        ip saddr @lan4 ip daddr @lan4 accept
        ip daddr 224.0.0.0/4 accept          # mDNS, SSDP
        ip daddr 255.255.255.255 accept
        ip daddr 169.254.0.0/16 accept

        # raw counters for the nightly drift check — never used to charge or
        # block; local destinations were accepted above, so WAN <-> LAN only
        ip saddr @lan4 update @devbytes { ip saddr }
        ip daddr @lan4 update @devbytes { ip daddr }

        # blocked subjects: let the nat chain explain, then nothing
        ip saddr @blocked4 tcp dport 80 accept
        ip saddr @blocked4 counter drop

        # no direct path to the ISP router
        ip saddr @lan4 ip daddr @router4 counter drop

        # QUIC off in v1: hostname is invisible
        ip saddr @lan4 udp dport 443 counter reject

        # everything else from the LAN goes through the proxy
        ip saddr @lan4 meta l4proto { tcp, udp } \
            meta mark set 0x1 tproxy to :7895 counter accept
    }

    chain dstnat {
        type nat hook prerouting priority dstnat; policy accept;

        # a blocked browser asking for any site gets the portal instead
        ip saddr @blocked4 tcp dport 80 redirect to :80
    }
}
```

```
ip rule add fwmark 0x1 lookup 100
ip route add local 0.0.0.0/0 dev lo table 100
```

}

## 11.3 Agent HTTP surface

| Path | Port | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /sub/<token>` | 80 | base64 subscription for one person |
| `GET /` | 80 | portal: device status, remaining bytes, subscription link |
| `GET /admin/...` | 8080 | persons, devices, routes (with rates), classes, periods, usage |
| `GET /admin/api/...` | 8080 | same, JSON, used by the UI |

Admin routes require a session cookie. The portal and `/sub/` are LAN-only and
token-gated; there is no login on port 80, so nothing sensitive lives there.
Admin is on a separate listener so it can later be moved behind TLS or an SSH
tunnel without touching the portal.
